name: Ocular Surface Squamous Neoplasia

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in individuals of African and equatorial regions

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnosis of OSSN

criteria.description: Presence of a conjunctival or corneal lesion with leukoplakic, gelatinous, or papilliform appearance
Histopathological confirmation of squamous epithelial dysplasia or invasive squamous cell carcinoma
Impression cytology showing atypical squamous cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical lesion consistent with OSSN plus histopathological confirmation of dysplasia or carcinoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires biopsy for definitive confirmation; clinical features guide initial suspicion.

pathognomonic.notes: White, plaque-like lesion on the ocular surface
Elevated, translucent lesion often at limbus

common.notes: Redness of the conjunctiva surrounding the lesion

common.symptomName: Ocular irritation or foreign body sensation
Corneal epithelial defects adjacent to lesion

common.notes: Raised, finger-like projections on lesion surface

occasional.notes: Tearing due to irritation or obstruction

rare.notes: Tumor extension into anterior chamber or cornea
Enlarged preauricular or submandibular lymph nodes
Extension of tumor into orbit causing proptosis

laboratory: Histopathology showing squamous epithelial dysplasia or invasive carcinoma
Impression cytology revealing atypical squamous cells
imaging: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing thickened, hyperreflective epithelium
Ultrasound biomicroscopy for assessing depth of invasion
genetic: No specific genetic markers routinely used; HPV DNA may be detected in some cases
other: Clinical slit-lamp examination revealing characteristic lesion morphology

distinguishingFeatures: Fleshy, triangular conjunctival growth extending onto cornea
Pigmented lesion rather than leukoplakic or gelatinous
Presence of melanin pigment on clinical exam and histology

redFlags: Invasion beyond conjunctiva into cornea or orbit
references: Lee GA, Hirst LW. Ocular surface squamous neoplasia. Surv Ophthalmol. 1995 Nov-Dec;39(6):429-50.
Karp CL, Moore JK, Galor A. Ocular surface squamous neoplasia: a review. Clin Exp Ophthalmol. 2016 Jan;44(1):1-10.
